newsitem.title: USA: Integon down after disappointing Q1.
newsitem.headline: Integon down after disappointing Q1.

text.p: Shares of Integon Corp fell more than 30 percent in early afternoon trading after the company reported disappointing results for the second straight quarter.
Integon reported a first quarter loss of $2.21 a share compared with a profit of $0.13 a share a year ago.
Excluding a $27.3 million after tax, or $1.73 a share, addition to loss reserves and a $2.4 million after tax, or $0.15 a share, writeoff, the company reported a first quarter loss of $0.33 a share.
That compares with the First Call consensus estimate for a loss of $0.03 a share.
Integon shares fell 4-1/8, or nearly 31 percent, to 9-1/4 in early afternoon.
The company also said it will retain Goldman Sachs to review its strategic alternatives, including a possible sale of the company.
Stephens Inc said it lowered its rating on Integon to hold from buy due to the poor results.
In his research note, analyst Brad Eichler said it appears as though Integon will "have to receive a relatively healthy bid to be even marginally beneficial for current shareholders."
This is the second straight quarter that the company has disappointed Wall Street.
In January, the company's shares fell about 15 percent after fourth quarter results fell short of expectations.
Integon said it has taken steps to improve future results.
The company said these actions include price increases, tightening of underwriting restrictions in certain states, and raising down payments on some of the company's premium payment plans.

"These actions are appropriate and should benefit financial results as we move forward," said chairman John Head III, who is also serving as chief executive officer following the resignation of James Lambie in November.
